thread.title: Amazon's stock falls into correction territory - MarketWatch

author: Tomi Kilgore
title: Amazon's stock falls into correction territory - MarketWatch
text:
Shares of Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, -3.50% dropped 3.2% in morning trade amid a broad selloff in the technology sector , to put them in danger of closing in correction territory for the first time since April. The stock has lost 11.2% since closing at a record $2,039.51 on Sept. 4. Many chart watchers believe a decline of at least 10% to up to 20% from a bull-market high defines a correction, while a decline of 20% or more is a bear market. A close at or below $1,835.55 would constitute a correction. On Monday, the stock hit an intraday low of $1,830.66 before bouncing to close above the correction threshold. In the previous correction, the stock had lost as much as 14.2% from its March 12, 2018 high of $1,598.39 to its April 2 closing low of $1,371.99; it climbed out of correction territory by the end of the month. Amazon is also in danger of ending the day with a market capitalization below $900 billion for the first time since Aug. 3. The market cap is currently $882.80 billion, below first-place Apple Inc.'s AAPL, -1.86% $1.07 trillion and above third-place Microsoft Corp.'s MSFT, -3.45% $833.92 billion. Amazon shares have still run up 54.8% year to date, while the Nasdaq Composite COMP, -2.15% has gained 9.8% and the S&P 500 SPX, -1.42% has tacked on 6.3%.
